analysis:
Examined the changes in ClusterSetupWizardLiveOperations.swift (head 563-565, 618, 625) and the additions to ClusterPublicModels.swift (head 21-24, 34-62, 139-163).

Wizard change: the local `discovery = discoveryMode(mtpMode, coordinator:)` was removed. readAutomatic now receives the raw mtpMode plus a `coordinator` flag (head 616-618, 623-625). Previously a coordinator-served setup always quoted the target only. It may now quote a speculative assistant that this build declares public for the artifact. The coordinator gating therefore moves into ClusterPlacementTensorAssistantSelection.readAutomatic/discoveryMode, which is not supplied. The targetFallback and fallbackWidening calls (630-636) use mode .off without `coordinator` and stay target-only. The explicit settings.tensorAssistants override path (608-614) is unchanged and is not coordinator-gated in this file. That path is pre-existing.

PublicModels: adds an optional tensorAssistant (nil for every model today). It adds ClusterPublicTensorAssistant, whose init requires a validated policy, singleton verification, a hash-syntax evidenceSHA256 and a docs/reports/*.md path. It also adds resourcePolicyFields, which fold the policy into resourcePolicySHA256. A @TaskLocal declarationOverride (test-only by comment) feeds `current`. tensorAssistant(runtimeModelID:artifactSHA256:) requires the tensorParallel family and qualifyingArtifact equality.

Security relevance: this concerns A-017/T-054 (which qualified build/policy may serve publicly) and T-007/T-056 (output correctness under speculative decoding). With every declared model nil today, the effective behavior is unchanged provided readAutomatic correctly returns nil/target-only under coordinator=true when no declaration exists. No regression is visible.

Integration must verify:
(1) readAutomatic/discoveryMode honors `coordinator` and consults ClusterPublicModels.tensorAssistant(for:) exactly, so the quoted policy equals the declared one.
(2) resourcePolicyFields is included in the native-start and release resource policy hash, so a mismatched assistant is refused.
(3) declarationOverride is never set by a product path. A TaskLocal is set only via withValue in code, so the risk is low.
(4) The evidenceSHA256-to-document equality is test-only, not checked at runtime.
